pr_title: Apply optimizations and fixes to Enumerable.Take(Range)
pr_body:
Makes the following changes to the new `Enumerable.Take(Range)` implementation:

* Separate `SizeOpt` and `SpeedOpt` implementations for non-`fromEnd` ranges.
* Optimize `fromEnd` ranges using `Enumerable.TryGetNonEnumeratedCount` to obtain the source count.
* Change enumerator disposal semantics to more closely follow the `TakeLast` and `SkipLast` implementations.
* Finally, expresses the `TakeLast` and `SkipLast` in terms of the `Take(Range)` implementation.

Fix #48631.

I've been investigating the seemingly unrelated [test failure](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/public/_build/results?buildId=1010618&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=31502058&resultId=146762&paneView=debug) affecting mono debug builds. The issue is caused by xunit's generic test parameter resolution logic: the removal of the private `SkipLastIterator` method seems to result in incorrect generic parameters being resolved for certain generic theory parameters. 

I have pushed a [commit](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/48634/commits/d7b11dab001b82cc533449c7f23e2bb90ec2515d) to demonstrate this and to further show that the failures are not due to a regression introduced by this PR, but rather a bug of xunit running over mono debug builds.
Hi @stephentoub @layomia, this is ready for review, would you be able to take a look?

issue_context.title: Optimize the implementation of LINQ partitioning APIs
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @eiriktsarpalis See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
My PR #48559 "Add LINQ APIs for Index and Range" was just merged, and this is a following up. @eiriktsarpalis @stephentoub ## Background: - LINQ internally use `IPartition` to optimize the implementation of partitioning operators, like `Take`, `Skip`, `ElementAt` - Later, more partitioning operators are added for LINQ, like `TakeLast`, `SkipLast`, `Take(System.Range)`, `ElementAt(System.Index)`. These new APIs are implemented by `yield return`. ## Proposal It is best to have an unified implementation of all the partitioning and element operators based on `IPartition`. ## Internal API changes Current `IPartition`: ```cs interface IPartition { TSource? TryGetElementAt(int index, out bool found); IPartition Take(int count); IPartition Skip(int count); // Other members ... } ``` 1. Update `IPartition` to support indexes from start or end: ```cs interface IPartition { // New members. bool TryGetElementAt(int index, bool isIndexFromEnd, [MaybeNullWhen(false)] out TSource element); IPartition Take(int startIndexInclusive, int endIndexExclusive, bool isStartIndexFromEnd, bool isEndIndexFromEnd); // Original members. TSource? TryGetElementAt(int index, out bool found) { found = TryGetElementAt(index, false, out TSource? element); return element; } IPartition Take(int count) => Take(0, count, false, false);; IPartition Skip(int count) => Take(count, 0, false, true); // Other members ... } ``` 2. Update all types that implement `IPartition`. All optimization code should be in these types, not in the LINQ operators. - `EmptyPartition` - `ListPartition` - `EnumerablePartition` - `RangeIterator` - `RepeatIterator` - `SelectArrayIterator` - `SelectRangeIterator` - `SelectListIterator` - `SelectIListIterator` - `SelectIPartitionIterator` - `SelectListPartitionIterator` - `OrderedPartition` - `OrderedEnumerable` 3. Implement `Enumerable.TakeIterator` based on `IPartition`, then use `Enumerable.TakeIterator` to implement `Take`, `Skip`, `TakeLast`, `SkipLast`, `Take(System.Range)`. 4. Update `ElementAt(System.Index)` to utilize `IPartitionTryGetElementAt` Then all partition and element APIs should be consolidated, optimized, consistent.
Author: Dixin
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Linq`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

This is related to #48634. Note that I did not add a Range method to `IPartition<T>` but combined the existing `Take` and `Skip` methods. Since most `IPartition<T>` implementations are slicing constructs, this might result in one intermediate allocation but should not have impact on enumeration performance.

review_comments: Why is this in a separate helper method?

It's simply there to tidy up readability of the parent method. Is it an issue?

FWIW @Dixin in #48631 proposed we add a `Take(int startIndex, int endIndex)` method to `IPartition<T>`  instead. I figured this approach is probably good enough, at the cost of one intermediate `IPartition<T>` allocation.
It's not an issue, it just seemed unnecessary when it could have just been an if block in the single method that calls it.
